# Purpose

This reproducible R Markdown notebook turns the two raw ZIP archives into **one row per team per match**, suitable for the group's exploratory analysis and regression models.

**Inputs:** `soccer_matches.zip` and `soccer_events.zip` (the five domestic leagues only).

**Outputs:** a clean CSV, data dictionary, validation summaries, a starter regression script, and an optional RDS file.

**Important measurement decision:** The supplied event files do **not** contain official possession percentages. We calculate `pass_share_pct`, each team's share of all pass events in its match, as a **possession proxy**. This is *not* official time-in-possession and should be labeled accordingly in the report. We also calculate `on_target_tagged` using Wyscout's accurate-event tag for shot attempts; this is a **tag-based shot-on-target proxy** that should be checked before treating it as an official shot-on-target count.

# 1. Packages and paths

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
required <- c("jsonlite", "dplyr", "tidyr", "purrr", "stringr", "readr",
              "tibble", "knitr")
missing <- setdiff(required, rownames(installed.packages()))
if (length(missing)) install.packages(missing, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
invisible(lapply(required, library, character.only = TRUE))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)

# Put both ZIP files in the same folder as this Rmd, or edit these paths.
matches_zip <- "soccer_matches.zip"
events_zip  <- "soccer_events.zip"
output_dir  <- "processed_data"
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

stopifnot(file.exists(matches_zip), file.exists(events_zip))
leagues <- c("England", "Spain", "Italy", "Germany", "France")
```

# 2. Read the original archives

```{r helpers}
find_zip_member <- function(zip_path, kind, league) {
  members <- utils::unzip(zip_path, list = TRUE)$Name
  pattern <- paste0("(^|/)", kind, "_", league, "\\.json$")
  candidates <- grep(pattern, members, value = TRUE)
  if (length(candidates) != 1L) {
    stop("Expected one ", kind, " file for ", league,
         "; found ", length(candidates), ".")
  }
  candidates
}

read_zip_json <- function(zip_path, member) {
  # unzip to a temporary directory: handles JSON arrays, not NDJSON
  tmp <- tempfile("wyscout_")
  dir.create(tmp)
  on.exit(unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE), add = TRUE)
  utils::unzip(zip_path, files = member, exdir = tmp)
  jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(tmp, member), simplifyVector = FALSE)
}

has_tag <- function(tags, id) {
  if (is.null(tags) || length(tags) == 0) return(FALSE)
  any(vapply(tags, function(x) identical(as.integer(x$id), as.integer(id)),
             logical(1)))
}

# Optional display names: parsed from match labels, while IDs remain the
# authoritative identifiers. Labels normally look like "Home - Away, 2 - 1".
parse_label_names <- function(label) {
  without_score <- sub(",\\s*[0-9]+\\s*-\\s*[0-9]+\\s*$", "", label)
  pieces <- strsplit(without_score, " - ", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (length(pieces) != 2) return(c(NA_character_, NA_character_))
  pieces
}
```

# 3. Extract match results: two rows per match

We use the **official score in the match file** as the response variable. Counting goal tags from events is not an adequate replacement because own goals and other edge cases can cause mismatches.

```{r match-extraction}
extract_matches <- function(league) {
  member <- find_zip_member(matches_zip, "matches", league)
  matches <- read_zip_json(matches_zip, member)

  purrr::map_dfr(matches, function(m) {
    sides <- m$teamsData
    if (length(sides) != 2L) return(tibble::tibble())
    team_rows <- purrr::map_dfr(sides, function(t) {
      tibble::tibble(
        team_id = as.integer(t$teamId),
        side = as.character(t$side),
        goals = as.integer(t$score)
      )
    })
    if (!setequal(team_rows$side, c("home", "away"))) {
      stop("Unexpected home/away sides in match ", m$wyId)
    }
    home_id <- team_rows$team_id[team_rows$side == "home"]
    away_id <- team_rows$team_id[team_rows$side == "away"]
    names <- parse_label_names(m$label)

    team_rows %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        match_id = as.integer(m$wyId),
        league = league,
        match_date = as.Date(substr(m$dateutc, 1, 10)),
        home = as.integer(side == "home"),
        opponent_id = ifelse(side == "home", away_id, home_id),
        team_name = ifelse(side == "home", names[1], names[2]),
        opponent_name = ifelse(side == "home", names[2], names[1]),
        goals_conceded = ifelse(side == "home",
                                team_rows$goals[team_rows$side == "away"],
                                team_rows$goals[team_rows$side == "home"])
      ) %>%
      dplyr::select(match_id, match_date, league, team_id, team_name,
                    opponent_id, opponent_name, home, goals, goals_conceded)
  })
}

match_data <- purrr::map_dfr(leagues, extract_matches)
stopifnot(nrow(match_data) == 3652L)
stopifnot(nrow(dplyr::distinct(match_data, match_id, team_id)) == nrow(match_data))
stopifnot(all(match_data$goals >= 0), all(!is.na(match_data$goals)))
knitr::kable(match_data %>% dplyr::count(league, name = "team_match_rows"))
```

# 4. Aggregate event records by match and team

Definitions:

- `shots`: all event records where `eventName == "Shot"` **or** `subEventName` is `"Free kick shot"` or `"Penalty"`.
- `on_target_tagged`: those shot attempts with tag `1801` (accurate). **Proxy**: validate its interpretation before calling it official shots on target.
- `passes_attempted`: all events with `eventName == "Pass"`.
- `passes_accurate`: passes tagged `1801`.
- `pass_accuracy_pct`: 100 × accurate passes / attempted passes.
- `pass_share_pct`: 100 × team passes / both teams' passes in that match; **not official possession**.

Set pieces such as throw-ins, goal kicks and corners are *not* counted as passes in this definition.

```{r event-extraction}
extract_events <- function(league) {
  member <- find_zip_member(events_zip, "events", league)
  events <- read_zip_json(events_zip, member)

  # Vectorized extraction is much faster than binding ~600k one-row tibbles.
  event_name <- vapply(events, function(e) e$eventName, character(1))
  sub_name <- vapply(events, function(e) e$subEventName, character(1))
  is_pass <- event_name == "Pass"
  is_shot <- event_name == "Shot" |
    sub_name %in% c("Free kick shot", "Penalty")
  keep <- which(is_pass | is_shot)
  rm(event_name, sub_name)

  event_rows <- tibble::tibble(
    match_id = vapply(events[keep], function(e) as.integer(e$matchId), integer(1)),
    team_id = vapply(events[keep], function(e) as.integer(e$teamId), integer(1)),
    passes_attempted = as.integer(is_pass[keep]),
    shots = as.integer(is_shot[keep]),
    accurate = vapply(events[keep], function(e) has_tag(e$tags, 1801L), logical(1))
  ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      passes_accurate = as.integer(passes_attempted == 1L & accurate),
      on_target_tagged = as.integer(shots == 1L & accurate)
    )
  rm(events)

  event_rows %>%
    dplyr::group_by(match_id, team_id) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      passes_attempted = sum(passes_attempted),
      passes_accurate = sum(passes_accurate),
      shots = sum(shots),
      on_target_tagged = sum(on_target_tagged),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Processing each league separately avoids loading all ~3 million events at once.
event_data <- purrr::map_dfr(leagues, function(league) {
  message("Processing events: ", league)
  gc(verbose = FALSE)
  extract_events(league)
})

stopifnot(nrow(dplyr::distinct(event_data, match_id, team_id)) ==
            nrow(event_data))
knitr::kable(event_data %>% dplyr::summarise(
  event_team_match_rows = dplyr::n(),
  shots = sum(shots),
  passes = sum(passes_attempted)
))
```

# 5. Join events to match results and create derived variables

Use a **left join** so that every team-match from the match files remains present. Missing event summaries are treated as missing, not automatically as zero.

```{r join-and-derive}
soccer_data <- match_data %>%
  dplyr::left_join(event_data, by = c("match_id", "team_id")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(match_id) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    match_passes = sum(passes_attempted, na.rm = TRUE),
    pass_share_pct = dplyr::if_else(
      !any(is.na(passes_attempted)) & match_passes > 0,
      100 * passes_attempted / match_passes,
      NA_real_
    ),
    pass_accuracy_pct = dplyr::if_else(
      !is.na(passes_attempted) & passes_attempted > 0,
      100 * passes_accurate / passes_attempted,
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(-match_passes) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(league, match_date, match_id, dplyr::desc(home))

stopifnot(nrow(soccer_data) == nrow(match_data))
stopifnot(nrow(dplyr::distinct(soccer_data, match_id, team_id)) ==
            nrow(soccer_data))
```

# 6. Validate the analysis-ready data

These checks are intended to **stop the pipeline** for structural problems and print warnings for statistics that need manual investigation.

```{r validations}
# Every match must have exactly two different teams and one home side.
match_checks <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(match_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    rows = dplyr::n(),
    home_count = sum(home),
    distinct_teams = dplyr::n_distinct(team_id),
    pass_share_total = sum(pass_share_pct),
    pass_share_missing = any(is.na(pass_share_pct)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(all(match_checks$rows == 2L))
stopifnot(all(match_checks$home_count == 1L))
stopifnot(all(match_checks$distinct_teams == 2L))

# Goals for a team must equal goals conceded by its opponent.
score_checks <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(match_id) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    reciprocal_scores = all(goals == rev(goals_conceded)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
stopifnot(all(score_checks$reciprocal_scores))

stopifnot(all(is.na(soccer_data$shots) |
                soccer_data$on_target_tagged <= soccer_data$shots))
stopifnot(all(is.na(soccer_data$passes_attempted) |
                soccer_data$passes_accurate <= soccer_data$passes_attempted))

valid_shares <- !match_checks$pass_share_missing
stopifnot(all(abs(match_checks$pass_share_total[valid_shares] - 100) < 1e-8))

missing_summary <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(
    dplyr::everything(), ~sum(is.na(.x)),
    .names = "missing_{.col}"
  )) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(),
                      names_to = "field", values_to = "missing_rows") %>%
  dplyr::filter(missing_rows > 0)

knitr::kable(missing_summary)
knitr::kable(soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(league) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    matches = dplyr::n_distinct(match_id),
    teams = dplyr::n_distinct(team_id),
    mean_goals = mean(goals),
    mean_shots = mean(shots, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_pass_share = mean(pass_share_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ))
```

```{r fix-team-names}
library(stringi)
library(dplyr)

# Decode literal Unicode escape sequences in team names
decode_team_name <- function(x) {
  vapply(x, function(name) {
    if (is.na(name)) return(NA_character_)

    # Only decode names containing literal Unicode escapes
    if (grepl("\\\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}", name)) {
      name <- stringi::stri_unescape_unicode(name)
    }

    name
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
}

# Update team and opponent names
soccer_data <- soccer_data %>%
  mutate(
    team_name = decode_team_name(team_name),
    opponent_name = decode_team_name(opponent_name)
  )

# Preview corrected names
soccer_data %>%
  distinct(team_name) %>%
  arrange(team_name) %>%
  print(n = 100)
```


```{r validate-team-names}
# Check for any remaining Unicode escape sequences
remaining_escapes <- soccer_data %>%
  filter(
    grepl("\\\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}", team_name) |
    grepl("\\\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}", opponent_name)
  )

cat("Rows with remaining Unicode escapes:",
    nrow(remaining_escapes), "\n")

# Stop knitting if any escaped names remain
stopifnot(nrow(remaining_escapes) == 0)

# Check specific examples
soccer_data %>%
  filter(
    grepl("Bayern|Atlético|Alavés", team_name)
  ) %>%
  distinct(team_name) %>%
  print()
```

## Manual spot checks

Select several matches (including 0–0 games and matches with penalties or own goals) and compare the computed statistics with the raw events. In particular, check whether tag `1801` on shots behaves like a true shots-on-target definition. A discrepancy does **not** change the official goals response; it means the shot proxy needs refinement.

```{r spot-checks}
set.seed(621)
sample_matches <- sample(unique(soccer_data$match_id), 5)
knitr::kable(soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::filter(match_id %in% sample_matches) %>%
  dplyr::select(match_id, league, team_name, opponent_name, home,
                goals, shots, on_target_tagged, passes_attempted,
                pass_accuracy_pct, pass_share_pct))
```


# 7. Additional quality checks and exploratory summaries

These checks are designed to identify potential measurement problems **before**
the group treats the engineered variables as established soccer statistics.
The plots below are exploratory only; they are not regression results.

## 7.1 Shot categories and accuracy-tag audit

Wyscout uses tag `1801` for an "accurate" event. For shots, that tag should
not automatically be equated with the official shots-on-target statistic.
This audit separates open-play shots, free-kick shots, and penalties, and
compares accuracy-tag counts with goal-tag counts (tag `101`) and save-related
tags. The event categories and tag meanings should be confirmed against the
Wyscout documentation before finalizing the metric.

```{r shot-audit}
audit_shots <- function(league) {
  member <- find_zip_member(events_zip, "events", league)
  events <- read_zip_json(events_zip, member)
  out <- purrr::map_dfr(events, function(e) {
    sub <- as.character(e$subEventName)
    if (!(identical(e$eventName, "Shot") ||
          sub %in% c("Free kick shot", "Penalty"))) return(NULL)
    tibble::tibble(
      league = league,
      match_id = as.integer(e$matchId),
      team_id = as.integer(e$teamId),
      shot_type = dplyr::case_when(
        sub == "Penalty" ~ "Penalty",
        sub == "Free kick shot" ~ "Free kick shot",
        TRUE ~ "Open-play shot"
      ),
      accurate_1801 = has_tag(e$tags, 1801L),
      goal_101 = has_tag(e$tags, 101L),
      # Keep the raw tag IDs for inspection rather than assuming meanings.
      tag_ids = paste(vapply(e$tags, function(t) as.character(t$id),
                             character(1)), collapse = ";")
    )
  })
  rm(events)
  out
}
shot_audit <- purrr::map_dfr(leagues, audit_shots)

shot_type_summary <- shot_audit %>%
  dplyr::group_by(league, shot_type) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    attempts = dplyr::n(),
    tagged_accurate = sum(accurate_1801),
    tagged_goals = sum(goal_101),
    goals_without_accurate_tag = sum(goal_101 & !accurate_1801),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(shot_type_summary)

# If any goals lack tag 1801, treating 1801 as all shots on target
# would necessarily miss those goals.
if (any(shot_type_summary$goals_without_accurate_tag > 0)) {
  warning("Some goal-tagged shots lack 1801; review shot-on-target definition.")
}

# Compare aggregate shot attempts with the final team-match table.
stopifnot(nrow(shot_audit) == sum(soccer_data$shots, na.rm = TRUE))
```

## 7.2 Spot-check raw shots, penalties and free kicks

The sample includes special shot types and goals where available. Use it to
inspect the raw tag combinations and confirm whether `on_target_tagged` should
be retained as a proxy or replaced with a better-defined variable.

```{r shot-spot-check}
set.seed(621)
shot_examples <- shot_audit %>%
  dplyr::group_by(shot_type, goal_101) %>%
  dplyr::group_modify(~dplyr::slice_sample(.x, n = min(5L, nrow(.x)))) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  dplyr::select(league, match_id, team_id, shot_type,
                accurate_1801, goal_101, tag_ids)
knitr::kable(shot_examples)
```

## 7.3 Team-name encoding audit

Team IDs are the authoritative keys. Match labels are display strings and
may contain encoding artifacts (for example `0e9` in place of an accented
character). This table flags suspicious names for manual correction.
Do not automatically substitute text into team identifiers.

```{r name-audit}
name_audit <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::distinct(team_id, team_name, league) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    suspicious_name = is.na(team_name) |
      stringr::str_detect(team_name, "[[:cntrl:]]|\\uFFFD|[[:alpha:]][0-9][a-fA-F][0-9a-fA-F][[:alpha:]]")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(suspicious_name)

knitr::kable(name_audit)
# Review the flagged rows and any names that look wrong in league tables.
# A separate, manually verified team-ID/name lookup is safest.
```

## 7.4 Numeric ranges, distributions and outliers

```{r distributions}
numeric_summary <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::select(goals, shots, on_target_tagged, passes_attempted,
                pass_accuracy_pct, pass_share_pct) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), names_to = "metric",
                      values_to = "value") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(metric) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(value)),
    minimum = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    p95 = unname(quantile(value, .95, na.rm = TRUE)),
    maximum = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(numeric_summary, digits = 2)

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))
hist(soccer_data$goals, main = "Goals per team-match", xlab = "Goals",
     breaks = seq(-0.5, max(soccer_data$goals) + 0.5, by = 1))
hist(soccer_data$shots, main = "Shot attempts", xlab = "Shots", breaks = 30)
hist(soccer_data$pass_accuracy_pct, main = "Pass accuracy",
     xlab = "Percent", breaks = 30)
hist(soccer_data$pass_share_pct, main = "Pass share proxy",
     xlab = "Percent", breaks = 30)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))

# High-value cases are for inspection, not automatic deletion.
extreme_matches <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(shots), dplyr::desc(goals)) %>%
  dplyr::select(match_id, league, team_name, opponent_name, home,
                goals, shots, on_target_tagged, pass_share_pct) %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 15)
knitr::kable(extreme_matches)
```

## 7.5 Predictor relationships

Shots and shots on target are naturally related. The correlation matrix is
a screening tool, not proof of problematic multicollinearity. Formal VIF and
model diagnostics belong in the regression analysis.

```{r predictor-checks}
predictor_correlations <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::select(shots, on_target_tagged, passes_attempted,
                pass_accuracy_pct, pass_share_pct) %>%
  stats::cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
knitr::kable(round(predictor_correlations, 3))

plot(soccer_data$shots, soccer_data$on_target_tagged,
     xlab = "Shot attempts", ylab = "Shots with tag 1801 (proxy)",
     main = "Shot metrics: relationship", pch = 16, cex = .35)
```

## 7.6 Home versus away analysis

These are **descriptive** comparisons. Differences in means do not establish
that playing at home causes the differences.

```{r home-away}
home_away_summary <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(league, home) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    team_matches = dplyr::n(),
    avg_goals = mean(goals, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_shots = mean(shots, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pass_accuracy = mean(pass_accuracy_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    avg_pass_share = mean(pass_share_pct, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(location = ifelse(home == 1L, "Home", "Away")) %>%
  dplyr::select(league, location, dplyr::everything(), -home)
knitr::kable(home_away_summary, digits = 2)

boxplot(goals ~ home, data = soccer_data, names = c("Away", "Home"),
        xlab = "Match location", ylab = "Goals scored",
        main = "Goals scored: home vs away")
```

## 7.7 Possession-proxy checks

`pass_share_pct` is deliberately defined as a **pass-share proxy** rather than
official ball possession. A useful validity check is whether it stays between
0 and 100 and whether both teams' shares add to 100 in every match.
Those checks confirm arithmetic consistency, **not** agreement with official
possession data. External possession observations would be needed for that.

```{r proxy-validation}
stopifnot(all(soccer_data$pass_share_pct >= 0 &
              soccer_data$pass_share_pct <= 100))
proxy_summary <- soccer_data %>%
  dplyr::group_by(league) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    min_pass_share = min(pass_share_pct),
    median_pass_share = median(pass_share_pct),
    max_pass_share = max(pass_share_pct),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(proxy_summary, digits = 2)
```

  "pass_accuracy_pct", "100 × accurate passes / attempted passes", "Derived", "NA if no passes",

                 file.path(output_dir, "soccer_home_away_summary.csv"))
readr::write_csv(numeric_summary,
                 file.path(output_dir, "soccer_numeric_summary.csv"))
readr::write_csv(missing_summary,
                 file.path(output_dir, "soccer_missingness.csv"))
readr::write_csv(match_checks,
                 file.path(output_dir, "soccer_match_validation.csv"))

starter <- c(
  "# DATA 621 — Starter regression analysis",
  "library(readr)",
  "library(dplyr)",
  "data <- read_csv('processed_data/soccer_team_match_2017_18.csv',",
  "                 show_col_types = FALSE)",
  "",
  "# pass_share_pct is a pass-share proxy, NOT official possession.",
  "# Only use complete cases for variables in each model.",
  "model_data <- data %>%",
  "  filter(!is.na(pass_share_pct), !is.na(pass_accuracy_pct),",
  "         !is.na(shots)) %>%",
  "  mutate(league = factor(league), team_id = factor(team_id))",
  "",
  "baseline <- lm(goals ~ pass_share_pct + shots + pass_accuracy_pct +",
  "                 home + league, data = model_data)",
  "summary(baseline)",
  "",
  "# Team fixed effects; omit league main effect (nested in team).",
  "team_adjusted <- lm(goals ~ pass_share_pct + shots +",
  "                      pass_accuracy_pct + home + team_id,",
  "                    data = model_data)",
  "summary(team_adjusted)",
  "",
  "# League-specific pass-share slopes with team fixed effects.",
  "league_interaction <- lm(goals ~ pass_share_pct +",
  "                         pass_share_pct:league + shots +",
  "                         pass_accuracy_pct + home + team_id,",
  "                       data = model_data)",
  "summary(league_interaction)",
  "",
  "# Count model: check dispersion and compare held-out performance later.",
  "poisson_model <- glm(goals ~ pass_share_pct + shots +",
  "                       pass_accuracy_pct + home + league,",
  "                     family = poisson(link = 'log'), data = model_data)",
  "summary(poisson_model)",
  "sum(residuals(poisson_model, type = 'pearson')^2) /",
  "  df.residual(poisson_model)",
  "",
  "# IMPORTANT: Split by match_id (not rows) before assessing",
  "# out-of-sample performance, since each match has two team rows."
)
writeLines(starter, file.path(output_dir, "starter_regression.R"))

cat("Files created in:", normalizePath(output_dir), "\n")
print(list.files(output_dir))

library(readr)

  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Check dimensions
dim(soccer_data)

# Check variables

# Check missing values
colSums(is.na(soccer_data))

# Preview dataset
soccer_data %>%
  select(
    league, team_name, opponent_name,
    home, goals, shots,
    pass_share_pct, pass_accuracy_pct
  ) %>%
  head(10) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
